_about: Every text CRANE-LLM shows to users, for both the JupyterLab extension and the %%crane_llm magic. Words in {braces} are filled in at runtime; keep them. After editing: run reload_crane_llm() in a notebook for the magic and the backend, and `jlpm build` in crane_llm/nb_extension, then refresh the browser, for JupyterLab.

toolbar.label: CRANE-LLM

commands.run_caption: Build the CRANE prompt from the active notebook cell and run the LLM
commands.toggle_caption: Include the live kernel state in the prompt. When off, only the executed cells and the target cell are sent.
commands.toggle_llm_caption: When you click CRANE-LLM: ask the LLM if the built-in checker finds no crash. When off, only the built-in checker runs and nothing is sent.
commands.toggle_guard_label: CRANE-LLM: Check Cells Before They Run
commands.toggle_guard_caption: Whenever you run a cell: run the built-in checker on it first, and do not run it if it will crash. The LLM is never used for this.

guard.label: Check cells before they run
guard.hint_on: The built-in checker checks each cell first, and a cell it finds will crash is not run. The LLM is never used for this.
guard.hint_off: Cells run without being checked. When on, only the built-in checker is used, never the LLM.
guard.verdict_label: not run, this cell would crash
guard.footer: Nothing in this cell was executed. To run it anyway, add the line `# crane: run` to it. To stop checking cells before they run, switch off "Check cells before they run" in JupyterLab, or run `%crane_llm guard off`.
guard.error: CRANE-LLM did not run this cell. {reasoning}
guard.magic_on: CRANE-LLM checks every cell before it runs, until the kernel restarts. A cell the built-in checker finds will crash is not run.
guard.magic_off: CRANE-LLM does not check cells before they run.
guard.magic_usage: Usage: %crane_llm guard on | %crane_llm guard off. To check a single cell, put %%crane_llm on its first line instead.
guard.unavailable_title: Cells in this notebook are not being checked

runinfo.hint_off: Prompt: executed cells and target cell only.

progress.no_finding: Built-in checker: no crash found. Asking the LLM...

verdict.title: CRANE-LLM: {label}
verdict.label_no_finding: no crash found by the checker
verdict.note_check: Crash found by CRANE-LLM's built-in checker, without calling the LLM. The cell will raise when it runs.
verdict.note_model_after_check: Predicted by the LLM. This is a prediction, and it can be wrong.
verdict.note_check_only: The built-in checker found no crash,  no LLM prediction was made. The cell may still crash: the checker only reports crashes it is certain of.

verdict.stale_explanation: A cell has run since this check, so the kernel state it was based on may have changed. Run the check again for a current prediction.

errors.missing_key_kaggle:
No API key found. On Kaggle, store it as a secret:

  1. In the notebook editor, open Add-ons > Secrets.
  2. Add a secret with the label CRANE_LLM_API_KEY and your key as the value.
  3. Tick the checkbox next to it, so this notebook may read it.

Then run the %%crane_llm cell again; no restart is needed. Keep the key
out of the notebook itself, which others can read once it is shared.
errors.missing_key_colab:
No API key found. On Colab, store it as a secret:

  1. Click the key icon in the left sidebar (Secrets).
  2. Add a secret named CRANE_LLM_API_KEY with your key as the value.
  3. Switch on 'Notebook access' for it.

Then run the %%crane_llm cell again; no restart is needed.
errors.missing_key:
No API key found. Set one up in any of these ways, then retry.

  1. From a notebook cell, saved to {path} for future sessions:
         import crane_llm
         crane_llm.set_api_key("sk-...")

  2. As an environment variable before starting Jupyter:
         CRANE_LLM_API_KEY=sk-...

  3. In a .env file in the directory you started Jupyter from:
         CRANE_LLM_API_KEY=sk-...

Any OpenAI-compatible provider works. For one that is not OpenAI, add a
base_url and a model, for example OpenRouter (Claude, Gemini and others
through a single key):
         crane_llm.set_api_key("sk-or-...",
                               base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1",
                               model="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5")

A local server needs no key at all, only a base_url:
         crane_llm.set_api_key(base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1",
                               model="qwen2.5-coder:32b")
